claim: An instance endpoint connects to a specific DB instance within an Aurora cluster, and each DB instance has its own unique instance endpoint.
question: What does an Aurora instance endpoint connect to?

values.display: connects to a specific DB instance
its own unique instance endpoint

evidence.quote: An instance endpoint connects to a specific DB instance within an Aurora cluster.
Each DB instance in a DB cluster has its own unique instance endpoint.

claim: In day-to-day Aurora operations, the main use of instance endpoints is to diagnose capacity or performance issues that affect one specific instance in an Aurora cluster.
question: What is the main day-to-day use of an Aurora instance endpoint?

values.display: diagnose capacity or performance issues
one specific instance

evidence.quote: In day-to-day Aurora operations, the main way that you use instance endpoints is to diagnose capacity or performance issues that affect one specific instance in an Aurora cluster.

claim: When some DB instances are configured differently from others, AWS recommends custom endpoints instead of the instance endpoint.
question: What does AWS recommend instead of an instance endpoint when DB instances are configured differently?

values.display: use custom endpoints instead of the instance endpoint
custom endpoints

evidence.quote: We recommend that you use custom endpoints instead of the instance endpoint in such cases.
Doing so simplifies connection management and high availability as you add more DB instances to your cluster.

claim: A custom endpoint for an Aurora cluster represents a set of DB instances that you choose, and Aurora balances connections among the instances in the group.
question: What does an Aurora custom endpoint represent?

values.display: represents a set of DB instances that you choose
custom endpoint

evidence.quote: A custom endpoint for an Aurora cluster represents a set of DB instances that you choose.
When you connect to the endpoint, Aurora performs connection balancing and chooses one of the instances in the group to handle the connection.

claim: An Aurora DB cluster has no custom endpoints until you create one, and you can create up to five custom endpoints for each provisioned Aurora cluster or Aurora serverless cluster.
question: How many custom endpoints can you create for each provisioned or Aurora serverless cluster?

values.display: up to five custom endpoints
no custom endpoints until you create one

qualifiers.scope: per provisioned Aurora cluster or Aurora serverless cluster

evidence.quote: An Aurora DB cluster has no custom endpoints until you create one. You can create up to five custom endpoints for each provisioned Aurora cluster or Aurora serverless cluster.

claim: You can define a custom endpoint to connect to instances that use a particular instance class or DB parameter group, for example to send internal users to low-capacity instances for reports and production traffic to high-capacity instances.
question: What is a typical use of an Aurora custom endpoint?

values.display: particular AWS instance class or a particular DB parameter group
instances that use a particular AWS instance class

evidence.quote: For example, you might define a custom endpoint to connect to instances that use a particular AWS instance class or a particular DB parameter group.
For example, you might direct internal users to low-capacity instances for report generation or ad hoc (one-time) querying, and direct production traffic to high-capacity instances.

claim: A custom endpoint provides balanced database connections based on criteria other than the read-only or read/write capability of the DB instances, unlike the reader endpoint.
question: How does a custom endpoint group instances differently from the reader endpoint?

values.display: criteria other than the read-only or read/write capability
balanced database connections

evidence.quote: The custom endpoint provides balanced database connections based on criteria other than the read-only or read/write capability of the DB instances.

claim: When you use custom endpoints, you typically do not use the reader endpoint for that cluster.
question: Do you typically use the reader endpoint of a cluster that uses custom endpoints?

values.display: typically don't use the reader endpoint
When you use custom endpoints

evidence.quote: When you use custom endpoints, you typically don't use the reader endpoint for that cluster.
This feature is intended for advanced users with specialized kinds of workloads where it isn't practical to keep all the Aurora Replicas in the cluster identical.

claim: Custom endpoints distribute connections across instances passively, using DNS to return the IP address of one of the instances randomly.
question: How do Aurora custom endpoints distribute connections across instances?

values.display: distribute connections across instances passively
using DNS to return the IP address of one of the instances randomly

evidence.quote: The custom endpoints distribute connections across instances passively, using DNS to return the IP address of one of the instances randomly.
If one of the DB instances within a group becomes unavailable, Aurora directs subsequent custom endpoint connections to one of the other DB instances associated with the same endpoint.

claim: With custom endpoints you can avoid updating CNAME records when your cluster grows or shrinks, and you can use encrypted TLS/SSL connections.
question: What advantages do custom endpoints have over DNS CNAME aliases?

values.display: avoid updating CNAME records
use encrypted Transport Layer Security/Secure Sockets Layer (TLS/SSL) connections

evidence.quote: By using custom endpoints, you can avoid updating CNAME records when your cluster grows or shrinks.
Custom endpoints also mean that you can use encrypted Transport Layer Security/Secure Sockets Layer (TLS/SSL) connections.

claim: Custom endpoints are not included in a snapshot, so you create them again after restoring a cluster.
question: Are custom endpoints included in a cluster snapshot?

values.display: Custom endpoints are not included in the snapshot
create them again after restoring

evidence.quote: Custom endpoints are not included in the snapshot. You create them again after restoring, and choose new endpoint names if the restored cluster is in the same region as the original one.

claim: Both reader and writer DB instances can be part of a custom endpoint of type ANY, and only reader DB instances can be part of a READER custom endpoint.
question: Which DB instances can be part of a READER custom endpoint and which of an ANY custom endpoint?

values.display: Both reader and writer DB instances can be part of an `ANY` custom endpoint
Only reader DB instances can be part of a `READER` custom endpoint

evidence.quote: Both reader and writer DB instances can be part of an `ANY` custom endpoint.
Only reader DB instances can be part of a `READER` custom endpoint.

claim: You cannot select the custom endpoint type in the console, and all custom endpoints created through the console have type ANY; you can set the type with the AWS CLI or Amazon RDS API.
question: Which custom endpoint type do endpoints created in the AWS Management Console get?

values.display: have a type of `ANY`
can't select the custom endpoint type in the AWS Management Console

evidence.quote: You can't select the custom endpoint type in the AWS Management Console. All the custom endpoints you create through the AWS Management Console have a type of `ANY`.

claim: When you add a DB instance to a custom endpoint or remove it from one, any existing connections to that DB instance remain active.
question: What happens to existing connections when you add or remove a DB instance from a custom endpoint?

values.display: existing connections to that DB instance remain active
add a DB instance to a custom endpoint

evidence.quote: When you add a DB instance to a custom endpoint or remove it from a custom endpoint, any existing connections to that DB instance remain active.

claim: A custom endpoint can have a list of DB instances to include (a static list) or to exclude (an exclusion list), and each custom endpoint can contain only one of these list types.
question: What kinds of membership lists can a custom endpoint use?

values.display: include in, or exclude from, a custom endpoint
static and exclusion lists

evidence.quote: You can define a list of DB instances to include in, or exclude from, a custom endpoint.
Each custom endpoint can contain only one of these list types.

claim: With the AWS CLI or Amazon RDS API you can specify the endpoint type, and for a READER custom endpoint the membership is automatically adjusted during failovers and promotions.
question: Does a READER custom endpoint adjust its membership automatically during failover?

values.display: endpoint membership is automatically adjusted during failovers and promotions
endpoint type is set to `READER`

evidence.quote: You can specify the endpoint type. Therefore, when the endpoint type is set to `READER`, endpoint membership is automatically adjusted during failovers and promotions.

claim: If an Aurora Replica becomes unavailable, it remains associated with any custom endpoints, but you cannot connect to it through those endpoints until it becomes available again.
question: Does an unavailable Aurora Replica stay associated with its custom endpoints?

values.display: remains associated with any custom endpoints
becomes unavailable

evidence.quote: If an Aurora Replica becomes unavailable, it remains associated with any custom endpoints.
However, you can't connect to it through those endpoints until it becomes available again.

claim: Aurora Replicas connect to the same storage volume as the primary DB instance, but support read operations only, and you use them to offload read workloads from the primary DB instance.
question: Which storage volume do Aurora Replicas connect to, and what do they support?

values.display: connect to the same storage volume as the primary DB instance
support read operations only

evidence.quote: Aurora Replicas connect to the same storage volume as the primary DB instance, but support read operations only.
You use Aurora Replicas to offload read workloads from the primary DB instance.

claim: You can add Aurora Replicas to a DB cluster using the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or the RDS API.
question: Which interfaces can you use to add an Aurora Replica to a DB cluster?

values.display: AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or the RDS API
add Aurora Replicas to a DB cluster

evidence.quote: You can add Aurora Replicas to a DB cluster using the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, or the RDS API.
